history.p: The presence of the 'WENLAV' watermark suggests that the Magnificat was composed sometime around 1730–35, that is while Scheibe was still living in Leipzig; it should be noted that the same type of paper was employed by Johann Sebastian Bach in the late 1720s. Indeed it was performed there at Neukirche in 1730–31, most likely commissioned by the church's cantor and organist, Carl Gotthelf Gerlach. In 1761 Breitkopf acquired the manuscript and performance material from the estate of Carl Gotthelf Gerlach, and at the end of the eighteenth century it was obtained by O.K.F. von Voß-Buch and listed as no. 286 in his thematic catalogue. However, it is apparently not listed in the Breitkopf sales catalogues though it is in the same folder as SchW B3:001 and Scheibe’s other Magnificats (SchW B2:003, B2:004, B2:007).

physDesc.watermark: an emblem, consisting of 'IMF' on a plaque and a leaping unicorn in two forms, is visible; the watermark is also found in Johann Sebastian Bach's church cantata, 'Es wartet Alles auf dich' dating from the late 1720s (Kobayashi, pp. 49–50; and Cammarota, Appendix C, nos. 29/29a). Paper of a dense quality.
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o; upright format, consisting of 4 nested bifolios; title page, blank page (folder), music (fols. 1r–8r), blank page with staves (fol. 8v); in all 4 bifolios. Hand-ruled paper, 25 staves on fols. 1r, 2r, 3r, 4v, 5r–v, 7r, 8r, 24 staves on fols. 1v, 2v, 3v, 6r–v, 7v, and 26 staves on fols. 4r (6 mm; single rastrum used) in light brown ink and music in black ink. A clean transcript copy with few changes in ink. Originally placed in the Breitkopf grey-blue folder including other works (fols. 79r–86v).

physDesc.watermark: three different watermarks are visible: 1) an emblem, consisting of 'IMF' on a plaque and a leaping unicorn in two forms, is seen in str., clrno., princ., timp. C., A., T., B.; the watermark is also found in Johann Sebastian Bach's church cantata, 'Es wartet Alles auf dich' dating from the late 1720s (Kobayashi, pp. 49–50; and Cammarota, Appendix C, nos. 29/29a); 2) 'WELENEAV/S', second pair of molds appears in fl., ob.1, bc., org. (Cammarota, Appendix C, no. 30); and 3) 'S' without the 'WENELAV' which seems to be the alternate form of the second pair of molds appears in the ob.2 (Cammarota, Appendix C, no. 30a). Paper of a fairly dense quality.
physDesc.physMedium: Sixteen instrumental and vocal parts in original grey-blue, O.K.F. von Voß-Buch limp folder; some of the instrumental parts have been restored. On folder in upper right-hand corner, ‘286. part.’ added in ink. Fifteen of the parts have been copied by Johann Ludwig Krebs while the transposing organ part has been made by Scheibe.
